items_missed: No 'How are you today?' and no time estimate on the agenda ('let's chat about it a bit' with no 'takes about 10-15 minutes' and no 'sound good?')
Never checked or confirmed availability for the September 10 move date
No pricing delivered on the call at all — no hourly rate, no included-items list, no 'pricing is super simple' opener, no 'no hidden fees' pitch. Everything deferred to a follow-up email

No No Worries Damage Coverage — a major miss on a call where the customer volunteered a China cabinet of 'very special, non-replaceable items like crystal and China' plus handmade furniture from her brother
No Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee
Entire Clock section skipped — no clock start, no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute increments
No Save Your Ass prep speech — no 'prep shortens the move and lowers the bill', no consolidation examples, no carload tip beyond a plant-specific aside
No typical time range and no crew/truck count, even though the customer explicitly needed a load/unload window to reserve the building's two-hour elevator block
No booking attempt on a self-declared 4th or 5th-time loyal customer ('you guys have been amazing, I'm staying loyal') — no 'want to lock that in?'
No bolded key-details list referenced for the email and no hours/how-to-reach-us
Loyalty discount request declined flatly with a policy explanation and no goodwill offset
Heavy filler and a long circular tangent re-explaining wardrobe boxes vs. gondolas stretched the call to 22.8 minutes with no price attached
top_strength: Outstanding discovery depth. She confirmed both addresses, square footage, floor and unit type up front, clarified what 'packing' actually means before quoting it, proactively asked about walk distance from the elevator to the unit, and handled every specialty item the customer raised — TV mount policy, plant liability waiver, glass desk, cacti — with a specific, confident answer. She also proactively offered to break the estimate out with and without packing, and steered the customer to the free gondola option over paid wardrobe boxes.
coaching_note: Give the price on the call. The discovery here was the best of the batch, but a 22-minute conversation with a loyal repeat customer ended with zero numbers spoken and no date held — deliver the hourly rate, the included list, and a rough time range live, then confirm it in the email. And with irreplaceable China and handmade furniture on the inventory, No Worries Damage Coverage was the single highest-value thing she could have said and never did.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm and personable — used 'Jen' repeatedly, built real rapport ('I can tell you came prepared, huh?' / 'Not my first rodeo'), and the customer stayed enthusiastic throughout; held back from a 5 by heavy filler and a flat response to the loyalty-discount ask.
